2608.02599.title: Bridging Artificial Intelligence and Power Systems Education Using a Hands-On Executable Framework
2608.02599.paper_summary: Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly central to power and energy systems, supporting modeling, forecasting, optimization, and control. Yet most existing works emphasize specialized applications and offer little reusable material for newcomers or interdisciplinary learners, who increasingly rely on large language models rather than building their own. This gap points to a need for engineering-grounded AI (EGAI), in which AI workflows follow established engineering and power-system domain rules rather than acting as task-agnostic black boxes. Motivated by a community survey of researchers and practitioners, which shows 92% report at least one barrier before running an AI model and 94% want a power-specific hands-on course. This paper presents a framework consisting of open, executable module library that lowers the entry barrier for AI in power systems. The modules follow a progressive difficulty ladder that maps core AI concepts onto representative power-system tasks: (i) foundational deep neural network (DNN) templates for function approximation and load-curve fitting; (ii) a domain-coupled convolutional neural network (CNN) power-flow surrogate for a 5-bus system; and (iii) frontier modules on DNN-assisted optimization, deep reinforcement learning (DRL) for battery storage control, and physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) for the swing equation. All modules are released as Jupyter notebooks that run locally or on Google Colab and are delivered through an IEEE online course and IEEE Power & Energy Society (PES) webinar series. The webinar drew more than 590 live attendees, which is among the ten most-attended IEEE PES webinars, and over 344 repository visits within two weeks, reinforcing the survey-based motivation.
2608.02599.paper_summary_zh: 人工智慧（AI）在電力和能源系統中日益重要，支持建模、預測、優化和控制。<lb/>然而，大多數現有的研究強調專門應用，並為新手或跨學科學習者提供的可重用材料有限，這些學習者越來越依賴大型語言模型，而不是自己構建模型。<lb/>這一差距顯示出對以工程為基礎的人工智慧（EGAI）的需求，其中AI工作流程遵循既定的工程和電力系統領域規則，而不是作為與任務無關的黑箱運作。<lb/>根據對研究人員和從業者的社區調查，92%的人報告在運行AI模型之前至少遇到一個障礙，94%的人希望有一個針對電力的實操課程。<lb/>本文提出了一個框架，包含開放的可執行模組庫，降低了AI在電力系統中的入門門檻。<lb/>這些模組遵循一個逐步的難度階梯，將核心AI概念映射到代表性的電力系統任務上：（i）用於函數逼近和負載曲線擬合的基礎深度神經網絡（DNN）模板；（ii）用於5母線系統的域耦合卷積神經網絡（CNN）功率流代理；以及（iii）有關DNN輔助優化、用於電池儲能控制的深度強化學習（DRL）和用於擺方程的物理知識神經網絡（PINNs）的前沿模組。<lb/>所有模組均作為Jupyter筆記本發布，可在本地或Google Colab上運行，並通過IEEE在線課程和IEEE電力與能源學會（PES）網路研討會系列提供。<lb/>該網路研討會吸引了超過590名現場參加者，是IEEE PES最受歡迎的十個網路研討會之一，並在兩週內獲得超過344次的資料庫訪問，進一步強化了基於調查的動機。
